logline: A prosecutor trainee becomes a murder suspect overnight, forcing the prosecutor who fired her to become her defense attorney - and slowly her closest ally.

renewal.note: Single-season legal romance thriller of 20 episodes concluded July 13, 2017. No sequel produced. The series is regularly cited as one of Ji Chang-wook's strongest pre-military service performances.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb audience rates it 7.7; Kdrama Kisses gave it 8.5/10 for its satisfying genre blend; critics praised Ji Chang-wook's performance and the serial killer thread, while noting pacing issues and filler in the second half.

pull_quotes.text: K-drama managed to combine a genuinely tense murder mystery with a sweet, silly romance and come up with entertaining results.
Ji Chang Wook and Nam Ji Hyun had such wonderful chemistry.

seasons.review_body: Suspicious Partner aired May to July 2017 on SBS, mixing legal procedural, serial killer thriller, and romantic comedy in a combination that reviewers described as a rarity in the K-drama landscape. Ji Chang-wook's Noh Ji-wook was praised across multiple outlets for the depth he brought to a character who communicates injury mostly through silence - The Fangirl Verdict noted his silently profound delivery of wordless moments communicated so much without dialogue. Nam Ji-hyun as Eun Bong-hee earned consistent praise for keeping the character likable through circumstances designed to test audience patience. The serial killer subplot was credited as simple but well-executed, and the show ends on a note that critics called genuinely satisfying. The standard caveats applied: pacing slackened in the second half, and some subplots accumulated filler weight that the first half did not suggest.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.review_body: Suspicious Partner Season 1 Episode 1 aired May 10, 2017 on SBS as the premiere of the 20-episode series. IMDb audience scored the season 7.7; Kdrama Kisses awarded it 8.5 out of 10. Nose in a Book described the show as a combination of 'a genuinely tense murder mystery with a sweet, silly romance.' The premiere positions the two leads as people already marked by prior heartbreak before staging the crisis that transforms their professional relationship overnight. The genre-blend of legal procedural, romantic comedy, and serial killer thriller is established within the first episode with enough tonal confidence that the shifts read as intentional rather than arbitrary. Ji Chang-wook's Noh Ji-wook arrives as a prosecutor whose silence and stillness communicate more than dialogue, and the premiere's central reversal - Bong-hee's overnight transformation from trainee to suspect - reframes the genre expectations cleanly.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere positions Noh Ji-wook and Eun Bong-hee as two people already connected by prior heartbreak before engineering the crisis that transforms their dynamic overnight. The genre-blend - workplace comedy, murder setup, romantic tension - is introduced with enough confidence that the tonal shifts feel purposeful rather than arbitrary.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Bong-hee's arrest at the end of the first episode: the pivot that reframes everything that seemed like a slow-burn romance as a legal emergency.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 20
episode_reviews.review_body: Suspicious Partner Season 1 Episode 20 aired July 13, 2017 on SBS as the series finale of the 20-episode run. IMDb audience scored the season 7.7; The Fangirl Verdict described Ji Chang-wook's performance as 'silently profound - he communicates so much without dialogue.' Nose in a Book called it 'a genuinely tense murder mystery with a sweet, silly romance.' The finale closes the serial killer investigation and the central romance in a manner that the show's critical record consistently described as more satisfying than the genre typically delivers. The courtroom resolution of the thriller arc is procedurally credible and the private resolution between Noh Ji-wook and Eun Bong-hee earns its emotional payoff through specificity rather than convention. The Fangirl Verdict noted 'a reasonably successful blend of crime and romance - a rarity in dramaland,' a verdict that holds for the finale, which maintains the tonal balance to the end.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale resolves the serial killer case and the central romance in a manner that critics called a genuine rarity: a satisfying conclusion in a genre that often disappoints. The emotional payoff between the leads lands because the show spent its run establishing their specific dynamic rather than depending on genre conventions alone.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The courtroom sequence that closes the serial killer arc and the private moment between the leads that follows it.

critic_note.text: A reasonably successful blend of crime and romance - a rarity in dramaland.
